_note: This is a WRITTEN EXAMPLE of a real Security Copilot promptbook structure, modeled on Microsoft's actual documented 'Microsoft Sentinel incident investigation' promptbook — it is NOT a captured Copilot session. No live Security Copilot license was available to run this for real, and that's stated here plainly rather than implied otherwise. The value of this file is showing the prompt sequence and reasoning, not a fabricated transcript.
modeledOn: Microsoft's real 'Microsoft Sentinel incident investigation' promptbook (see Microsoft Learn: Use promptbooks in Microsoft Security Copilot)
triggerScenario: An incident fires from detections/kql/password-spray-pattern.kql — this promptbook is what an analyst would run against it.

promptSequence.prompt: Summarize incident [incident-number] — what happened, which accounts were targeted, and over what time window?
promptSequence.expectedOutputShape: Plain-language summary: source IPs, target account count, spray pattern (many accounts, few attempts each) vs. brute force (few accounts, many attempts) distinction, time window.

promptSequence.prompt: Cross-reference the source IPs in this incident against our threat intel watchlist and known threat actor infrastructure.
promptSequence.expectedOutputShape: Matches (or explicit non-matches) against threat-intelligence/sentinel-ti-watchlist.json, plus any public threat-actor infrastructure overlap Copilot's own TI sources surface.

promptSequence.prompt: For any accounts with a successful sign-in in this incident, check Conditional Access policy compliance and Intune device compliance status.
promptSequence.expectedOutputShape: Ties directly to this project's CA001/CA003 policies and Intune baseline — confirms whether the layered defense actually held, not just whether the attack was detected.

promptSequence.prompt: Generate an executive summary of this incident suitable for a non-technical stakeholder, including remediation actions taken.
promptSequence.expectedOutputShape: Plain-language report referencing the SOAR-Disable-Compromised-User playbook's outcome if it fired.

totalEstimatedCost: ~5 SCUs per full run, per Microsoft's published complexity tiers — cited in this project's README, not invented
